channel.title: Tal Paperin Insights
channel.description: Field notes on B2B sales, fractional CRO leadership, go-to-market and fixing broken revenue.

item.title: If Your Company Might Only Last Six Months, Your Sales Math Changes
item.description: A CTech opinion argues your next business might last six months, and that can be enough. If that is the bet, sell for fast payback, not distant lifetime value.

item.title: When the Channel That Feeds You Changes, Your Revenue Is Exposed
item.description: AI is changing how hotels reach travelers, and a $25M round followed. If one channel feeds most of your revenue, you do not own your demand.

item.title: "A Culture of Failing to Keep Promises" Is a Sales Problem
item.description: An investor described Sapiens as having a culture of failing to keep promises. That starts in sales, when reps oversell to hit quota and delivery pays.

item.title: 40 Companies, One Category, 20 of Them Israeli. How Do You Sell?
item.description: Nikesh Arora counts 40 firms racing to secure AI agents, at least 20 Israeli. When the category is a knife fight, the deck does not win. The sales motion does.

item.title: Debt Does Not Kill Companies. Soft Revenue Plus Debt Does.
item.description: Analysts warn that debt could amplify the damage AI does to businesses. The real risk is debt stacked on revenue that was never durable. Fix the revenue first.

item.title: HubSpot Cut 660 Jobs and Called It AI. Read It Differently.
item.description: HubSpot cut nearly 660 jobs and HoneyBook cut 14%, both blamed on AI. The honest read: AI gave cover to trim headcount a weak sales engine had carried.

item.title: At-Bay Was Valued at $1.35B. It Sold for $575M. Read the Gap.
item.description: At-Bay hit a $1.35B valuation and sold to Munich Re for $575M. A valuation is a bet. Revenue is a fact. Here is how founders should read the difference.

item.title: Product-Led vs Sales-Led Growth: Which Does Your B2B Need?
item.description: PLG fits low-ACV self-serve products. Sales-led fits high-ACV committee buying. Most B2B need a hybrid. Choose by buyer, price, and complexity, not by hype.

item.title: The Sales Metrics Founders Should Actually Track
item.description: Founders drown in dashboards. Here are the five sales metrics that predict revenue, the vanity numbers to ignore, and when each one should make you act.

item.title: In-House SDRs vs Outsourced: What Early-Stage B2B Should Do
item.description: In-house SDRs give control but are slow and costly to build. Outsourced and pay-per-meeting give speed and results-based cost. Here is how to choose by stage.

item.title: How to Write a Cold Email That Actually Books Meetings
item.description: Most cold email fails because it leads with the product. Here is the framework I use to write short, relevant emails that book real B2B meetings.

item.title: Why Deals Stall at the Proposal Stage (and How to Unstick Them)
item.description: A proposal is not a close. Deals stall because you sent a price before you built consensus and urgency. Here is how to fix it before the proposal goes out.

item.title: Enterprise Sales for Startups: Selling to Companies 100x Your Size
item.description: Selling to giants means committees, procurement, and long cycles. Land a champion, multi-thread the account, de-risk the buy, and never single-thread.

item.title: How to Recruit Channel Partners That Actually Sell
item.description: Most partnerships produce nothing. Recruit partners for real fit and motivation, enable them properly, hold them to numbers, or cut them.

item.title: How Much Pipeline You Really Need to Hit Your Number
item.description: Pipeline coverage is quota divided by win rate, adjusted for cycle time. Most teams undercount because the pipeline is stuffed with dead deals.

item.title: How to Set Sales Quotas Your Team Can Actually Hit
item.description: A quota nobody hits demotivates your team and hides the real problem. Here is how to build quotas bottoms-up from rep capacity and pipeline math.

item.title: Sales Comp Plans That Actually Motivate
item.description: A good comp plan is simple enough a rep can calculate their own check. Here is how to set base, variable, OTE, and quota by role, and the mistakes to avoid.

item.title: $4.6B in Revenue. An $8B Loss. A Possible $2 Trillion Valuation.
item.description: Anthropic makes $4.6B, loses $8B+ operating, and could be worth $2 trillion. Three numbers that shouldn't fit together, and in 2026 somehow do.

item.title: OpenWeb Raised $390M and Hit a $1.5B Valuation. Now It's Seeking Insolvency Protection.
item.description: OpenWeb raised $390M at a $1.5B valuation and now seeks insolvency protection. The lesson for founders: fix the revenue machine while you still have runway.

item.title: How to Scale From Founder-Led Sales to a Real Sales Team
item.description: Founder-led sales does not scale by hiring. Codify the founder's motion into a playbook, hire to that profile, install management and cadence. Order matters.

item.title: Why Your Demos Don't Close
item.description: Demos fail when they come before discovery, because you are showing features to a problem you never uncovered. Sell the problem first, then demo to the pain.

item.title: How Long Should a B2B Sales Cycle Be (and How to Shorten Yours)
item.description: Most B2B sales cycles are long because of stalls and weak qualification, not real complexity. Here are honest benchmarks and the two moves that shorten cycles.

item.title: Intel Almost Killed RealSense. Then It Fixed Its Sales and Sold for $600M.
item.description: Intel nearly shut RealSense down. Spun out, it went from $8M a quarter to a $600M sale. The technology did not change. The way it sold did.

item.title: Outbound vs Inbound for Early-Stage B2B: Where to Start
item.description: Inbound compounds but takes many months. Outbound buys control, speed, and market knowledge now. Here is why early-stage B2B almost always needs outbound first.

item.title: How to Forecast Revenue When You Have No Sales History
item.description: No sales history? A top-down wish is not a forecast. Here is how to build a bottoms-up revenue model from activity and conversion assumptions you can defend.

item.title: Your First Sales Hire Keeps Failing. Here Is Why.
item.description: If your first sales hire failed and the second is struggling, look at the system before the rep: wrong profile for your stage, no playbook, no management.

item.title: How to Build a B2B Sales Process From Scratch
item.description: A CRM with random stages is not a sales process. How to build a real B2B sales process from scratch, with buyer-based stages and a forecast you can trust.

item.title: How to Hand Off Founder-Led Sales Without Killing the Pipeline
item.description: Most founder-led sales handoffs fail because founders dump leads on a rep with no motion. Here is how to transfer the sale without killing your pipeline.

item.title: Why Your Startup Can't Sell (And It's Not the Product)
item.description: Most founders blame the product when sales stall. The real problem is almost always the motion around it. Here is how to tell, and what to fix first.

item.title: When to Hire Your First Salesperson (Founders Wait Too Long, Then Panic)
item.description: Revenue milestones do not tell you when to hire your first salesperson. A repeatable motion you can hand off does. Here is what ready actually looks like.
